text: At Chernobyl, pressing the emergency shutdown button made the reactor more powerful, for a few seconds.
Each control rod was boron on top, to swallow neutrons. But below it hung a long piece of graphite.
That night, the rods had been pulled almost all the way out.
So when the button sent them back in, the graphite slid into the bottom of the core first, pushing out water that had been soaking up neutrons.
Power jumped at the bottom of the core. And the rods were slow, around eighteen seconds to go all the way in.
The reactor didn't last that long. Full video on my channel.
